criteria.text: `Term` (`src/ui/format.ts`) has an optional `community?: number | null` field typed as a plain `number`, never a type imported from `src/communities.ts`; `pnpm typecheck` passes with a `Term` built with and without that field.

`communityRanking` returns the top 6 distinct non-null communities by node count descending, ties broken by ascending community id — pinned with a hand-built `Term[]` fixture carrying more than 6 distinct communities of varying sizes, including a tie.

`themeMask` returns `null` for a term whose `community` is `null` or `undefined`; `` `var(--theme-${rank})` `` for a term in the top 6 of a given ranking; and `null` (not a literal muted string) for a non-null community outside the top 6 — each case pinned by a direct call, no DOM.

`paintSelection` accepts `MaskState`; `'avaliacao'` sets `is-masked` and not `is-themed` (unchanged: still requires a person mean, exactly as today's boolean path does); `'tema'` sets `is-themed` and not `is-masked`; `'off'` sets neither — asserted via `test/fake-dom.ts` classList state.

`wordMarkup` and `paintColumns` emit a `--theme` inline style only when `themeMask` is non-null for that node, in addition to (never instead of) any `--mask` style already present, exercised the same way the current `--mask` assertions in `test/render.test.ts` are.
`drawMap`'s `ranking` parameter reaches `wordMarkup` for every placed node — a graph with a top-6 community produces at least one `--theme` style in the painted SVG.

`inspect()` renders a "no mesmo tema" list only when all three hold: mask state is `'tema'`, the focused term's `community` is non-null, and at least one other node on the map shares it; absent in every other combination, including a focused term whose `community` is `null`.

Each community-mate entry in that list is reachable and actionable via `onChoose`, exercised through the same click/keyboard contract `test/render.test.ts` already uses for `.related`/`relatedButtons` entries, not a raw DOM query.

`handlers.mask` (the renamed `toggleMask` path in `src/ui/figures/atlas.ts`) cycles `'avaliacao' → 'tema' → 'off' → 'avaliacao'` in that fixed order and wraps — exercised through `createHandlers`, not a click on static HTML.
`#mask`'s label text and `aria-pressed` update on every cycle step (`"Colorir por avaliação"`/`true`, `"Colorir por tema"`/`true`, `"Sem cor"`/`false`).

The control stays `hidden` whenever `mode === 'strip'`, and the previously chosen mask state (avaliação/tema/off) is preserved across a switch into and back out of `'strip'` mode — extending the existing strip-mode test in `test/figures-atlas.test.ts`.

`src/ui/api.ts`'s `params()` includes `communities: '1'` in every call, alongside the existing `testimony: '1'` — pinned in `test/api.test.ts` beside the existing `assert.equal(p.get('testimony'), '1')` assertion.

When every node in the current graph has `community` either `null` or the field absent from the payload entirely, `'tema'` state paints every word with `--muted` (no `--theme` style emitted) and the tema key states the build has no communities for this recorte — wording that names build coverage, not a document-count floor, distinguishing it from the evaluation mask's `MASK_MIN` copy in the assertion itself (not merely by eyeballing the two strings).

`atlas.css` defines `--theme-1` through `--theme-6` as six values on `:root`, no two equal to each other or to `--hostile`/`--favor`/`--cmp-a`/`--cmp-b`, each meeting a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against `--bg` — checked by a relative-luminance/contrast-ratio computation over the literal hex values, not by eyeballing.

No existing evaluation-mask behaviour changes outcome: every pre-existing assertion in `test/render.test.ts` and `test/figures-atlas.test.ts` about `is-masked`, `#maskLegend`, `termMask`, or `MASK_MIN` still passes once updated only for the boolean→`MaskState` signature change (a mechanical rename of `mask: true` to `mask: 'avaliacao'` at call sites, never a change to what is asserted).

`test/invariants.test.ts` continues to pass unmodified: every new markup path (`themeLegend`, the inspector's community-mates list, the new `--theme` style attributes) goes through `format.ts`'s `html` tag, nothing feeds `innerHTML` a bare template literal.
